newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MIM says profit could be sharply cut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MIM says profit could be sharply cut.

text.p: Base metals miner MIM Holdings Ltd said on Thursday that the profitability of its core operations at Mount Isa in central Queensland could be cut by more than A$200 million this fiscal year if the fall in copper prices and the rise in the Australian dollar is sustained.

"Despite all the improvements in costs and productivity, we have experienced the double hit of sharply lower copper prices and higher exchange rates," Phil Wright, the executive general manager, Mount Isa operations, said in a speech to the annual meeting.

"These two factors alone - a 35 percent fall in the copper price and a three percent rise in the exchange rate - if sustained for a full year will affect our results by over A$200 million at Mount Isa," Wright said.

"Following more than 12 months of detailed feasibility study we announced a A$500 million investment in our copper business to keep Mount Isa as a major profit earner for MIM well into the next century," he said.
Mt Isa had extensive copper reserves consisting of 66 million tonnes of reserves and another 60 million tonnes of resources, grading from 2.7 percent to 4.1 percent copper.

Wright said one major decision facing the company at Mt Isa was the future of lead-zinc mining, with the key issue being how to develop the George Fisher zinc/lead/silver deposit located 22 km away and adjacent to the operating Hilton Mine.
